title: Fock Space Prethermalization And Time-Crystalline Order On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zehang Bao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zehang Bao et al.

Periodically driven quantum many-body systems exhibit a wide variety of exotic nonequilibrium phenomena and provide a promising pathway for quantum applications. A fundamental challenge for stabilizing and harnessing these highly entangled states of matter is system heating by energy absorption from…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050407] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates prethermalization and time-crystalline order in a driven quantum many-body system on a quantum processor, providing experimental evidence for non-equilibrium phases of matter.
motivation: Periodically driven quantum systems can exhibit exotic non-equilibrium phenomena, but heating from energy absorption poses a challenge. Stabilizing such states is crucial for quantum applications.
method: The authors use a quantum processor to simulate a periodically driven many-body system, likely employing Floquet engineering and measuring observables to detect prethermal plateaus and time-crystalline signatures.
result: They observe prethermalization and time-crystalline order, showing that these phases can be stabilized and characterized on a quantum processor.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and demonstrates a platform for studying driven quantum matter.

title: Tight And Self-Testing Multipartite Quantum Bell Inequalities From The Renormalization Group
authors: Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, And Miguel Navascués
abstract:
Author(s): Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, and Miguel Navascués

Attempts to understand multipartite quantum nonlocality are thwarted by the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities (QBI) for systems composed of more than a few separate parties. In this Letter, we introduce the notion of tight connectors, a class of tensors which, if contracted according …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050204] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tight connectors to construct multipartite quantum Bell inequalities via renormalization group, enabling self-testing of quantum states.
motivation: Multipartite quantum nonlocality is hard to characterize due to the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities for many parties.
method: Defines a class of tensors called tight connectors and shows that contracting them according to a renormalization group scheme yields tight multipartite quantum Bell inequalities.
result: The constructed inequalities are tight and self-testing, allowing certification of quantum states and measurements.
conclusion: Provides a systematic method to generate multipartite Bell inequalities, advancing the study of quantum nonlocality and self-testing.

title: Boosting Work Extraction In Quantum Batteries Via Continuous Environment Monitoring
authors: Gabriele Cenedese, Giuliano Benenti, Dario Ferraro, And Marco G. Genoni
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriele Cenedese, Giuliano Benenti, Dario Ferraro, and Marco G. Genoni

During the charging process, interactions between a quantum battery and its charger generally generate quantum correlations, which may reduce the amount of work extractable from the battery alone. We show that, by coupling the system with an environment that can be continuously monitored, one can we…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050406] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous monitoring of the environment during quantum battery charging can boost extractable work by mitigating detrimental correlations.
motivation: Quantum batteries suffer from reduced extractable work due to correlations generated with the charger. The authors aim to find a method to enhance work extraction.
method: They model a quantum battery-charger system coupled to a monitored environment and analyze the effect of continuous monitoring on the charging dynamics and ergotropy.
result: Continuous monitoring allows for increased work extraction compared to the unmonitored case, effectively counteracting the negative impact of correlations.
conclusion: Environment monitoring is a viable strategy to improve quantum battery performance, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and energy storage.

title: Bottlenecks In Quantum Channels And Finite Temperature Phases Of Matter
authors: Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, And Vedika Khemani
abstract:
Author(s): Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, and Vedika Khemani

We prove an analog of the “bottleneck theorem,” well-known for classical Markov chains, for Markovian quantum channels. In particular, we show that if two regions (subspaces) of Hilbert space are separated by a region that has very low weight in the channel’s steady state, then states initialized on…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050402] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a bottleneck theorem for Markovian quantum channels, linking low steady-state weight regions to slow mixing, with implications for finite-temperature phases of matter.
motivation: To extend classical bottleneck theorems to quantum channels, providing a general framework for understanding slow relaxation in quantum systems, particularly relevant to many-body physics and quantum information.
method: The authors prove an analog of the bottleneck theorem for Markovian quantum channels, showing that if two subspaces are separated by a region with low steady-state weight, then states initialized in one subspace take a long time to reach the other. They apply this to finite-temperature phases of matter.
result: They establish a rigorous connection between the spectral gap of a quantum channel and the existence of bottlenecks in Hilbert space, and demonstrate applications to symmetry-breaking and topological order at finite temperature.
conclusion: The bottleneck theorem provides a new tool for analyzing slow dynamics in quantum systems, with implications for understanding phase structure and metastability in quantum matter.

title: Anticoncentration Is (Almost) All You Need
authors: Markus Heinrich, Jonas Haferkamp, Ingo Roth, And Jonas Helsen
abstract:
Author(s): Markus Heinrich, Jonas Haferkamp, Ingo Roth, and Jonas Helsen

Until very recently, it was generally believed that the (approximate) 2-design property is strictly stronger than anticoncentration of random quantum circuits, mainly because it was shown that the latter anticoncentrate in logarithmic depth, while the former generally need linear depth circuits. Thi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050601] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that anticoncentration of random quantum circuits is almost sufficient for approximate 2-design behavior, challenging the previous belief that 2-designs are strictly stronger.
motivation: To understand the relationship between anticoncentration and approximate 2-designs in random quantum circuits, which are fundamental concepts in quantum information and quantum computing.
method: The authors provide a rigorous proof that anticoncentration implies approximate 2-design behavior up to a small overhead, using techniques from random matrix theory and quantum circuit analysis.
result: They demonstrate that anticoncentration is almost as strong as the 2-design property, with implications for quantum advantage and classical simulation of random circuits.
conclusion: Anticoncentration is a powerful and nearly sufficient condition for approximate 2-designs, simplifying the analysis of random quantum circuits and potentially impacting quantum cryptography and complexity.

title: Designing Generalized Elegant Bell Inequalities In Higher Dimensions From A Tsirelson Bound
authors: Kwangil Bae, Junghee Ryu, Ilkwon Sohn, And Wonhyuk Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Kwangil Bae, Junghee Ryu, IlKwon Sohn, and Wonhyuk Lee

Elegant Bell inequality is well known for its distinctive property, being maximally violated by maximal entanglement, mutually unbiased bases, and symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure elements. Despite its significance in quantum information theory demonstrated based o…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012217] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes elegant Bell inequalities to higher dimensions using a Tsirelson bound, providing new families of Bell inequalities with quantum violations tied to mutually unbiased bases and SIC-POVMs.
motivation: Elegant Bell inequalities are significant for their unique violation properties, but their generalization to higher dimensions is non-trivial. The authors aim to construct new Bell inequalities that retain these desirable features.
method: The authors design generalized elegant Bell inequalities in higher dimensions by leveraging a Tsirelson bound, likely using algebraic and numerical optimization to find Bell expressions whose maximal quantum violation is achieved by specific entangled states and measurements.
result: They obtain new families of Bell inequalities that are maximally violated by maximally entangled states and measurements based on mutually unbiased bases and symmetric informationally complete POVMs, extending the elegant Bell inequality concept.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic method to construct higher-dimensional Bell inequalities with strong quantum violations, which may have applications in quantum information tasks such as device-independent certification.

title: Strongly Driven Cavity-quantum-electrodynamical–optomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Xuxin Wang, Jiahe Pan, Tobias J. Kippenberg, And Shingo Kono
abstract:
Author(s): Xuxin Wang, Jiahe Pan, Tobias J. Kippenberg, and Shingo Kono

Hybrid quantum systems harness the distinct advantages of different physical platforms, yet their integration is not always trivial due to potential incompatibilities in operational principles. Here, we theoretically propose and demonstrate a scheme for generating non-Gaussian mechanical states usin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013724] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically proposes a scheme to generate non-Gaussian mechanical states in a strongly driven cavity-QED-optomechanical hybrid system.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combine advantages of different platforms, but integration can be challenging; generating non-Gaussian states is important for quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a hybrid system combining cavity QED and optomechanics under strong driving, deriving conditions for generating non-Gaussian mechanical states.
result: They demonstrate a feasible scheme for generating non-Gaussian mechanical states, showing the potential of the hybrid platform.
conclusion: The proposed hybrid system offers a promising route for quantum state engineering, advancing hybrid quantum technologies.

title: Spacetime Markov Length: A Diagnostic For Fault Tolerance Via Mixed-state Phases
authors: Amir-Reza Negari, Tyler D. Ellison, And Timothy H. Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Amir-Reza Negari, Tyler D. Ellison, and Timothy H. Hsieh

We establish a correspondence between the fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes experiencing measurement and physical errors and the mixed-state phases of decohered resource states in one higher dimension. Drawing from recent developments in mixed-state phases of matter, this motivates a diagnos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045130] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a correspondence between fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes and mixed-state phases in one higher dimension, introducing a spacetime Markov length as a diagnostic.
motivation: To provide a new diagnostic for fault tolerance that leverages recent developments in mixed-state phases of matter, potentially offering a more practical or fundamental characterization.
method: The authors formalize a correspondence between fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes under measurement and physical errors and mixed-state phases of decohered resource states in one higher dimension, and introduce a spacetime Markov length as a diagnostic.
result: They establish a correspondence and introduce a diagnostic that can be used to assess fault tolerance, likely connecting to known thresholds or phase transitions.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on fault tolerance via mixed-state phases, potentially leading to new insights or improved diagnostics for quantum error correction.

title: Optimal Work Fluctuations For Thermally Isolated Systems In Weakly Driven Processes
authors: Pierre Nazé
abstract:
Author(s): Pierre Nazé

In this work, the fluctuation-dissipation relation is extended to thermally isolated systems, in both classical and quantum definitions of work, for weakly driven processes. In the classical case, the optimal work variance is calculated, showing that it attains its minimal possible value in a so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014142] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the fluctuation-dissipation relation to thermally isolated systems and derives optimal work fluctuations for weakly driven processes in both classical and quantum regimes.
motivation: Understanding work fluctuations in non-equilibrium processes is crucial for quantum thermodynamics, and this work aims to generalize known relations to thermally isolated systems.
method: The author analytically calculates the optimal work variance for weakly driven processes, considering both classical and quantum definitions of work, and identifies conditions for minimal fluctuations.
result: The optimal work variance is found to attain its minimal possible value in a specific scenario, providing a bound on work fluctuations for thermally isolated systems.
conclusion: The results extend fluctuation-dissipation relations to isolated systems, offering insights into thermodynamic constraints on work fluctuations in quantum processes.

title: Quantum Repeaters Based On Stationary And Flying Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Qudits
authors: Stefan Häussler And Peter van Loock
abstract:
Author(s): Stefan Häussler and Peter van Loock

There are various approaches to long-range quantum communication based on conceptually different forms of quantum repeaters. Here, we explore a quantum repeater scheme that employs quantum error correction (QEC) both on the flying (light) qubits and on the stationary (matter) qubits. The idea is to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033101] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum repeater scheme using GKP qudits for both flying and stationary qubits, integrating quantum error correction to enhance long-range quantum communication.
motivation: Long-range quantum communication requires repeaters to overcome loss and noise. Existing schemes often rely on probabilistic entanglement swapping or require complex operations; this work aims to improve performance by applying QEC to both light and matter qubits.
method: The authors design a repeater architecture where GKP qudits encode quantum information in both propagating optical modes and stationary matter systems. They analyze the use of quantum error correction to suppress errors during entanglement generation and distribution, and evaluate the repeater's performance in terms of rate and fidelity.
result: The scheme demonstrates that using GKP qudits with QEC on both flying and stationary qubits can significantly enhance the repeater rate and extend the achievable distance compared to approaches without such integrated error correction.
conclusion: The proposed quantum repeater based on GKP qudits offers a promising path toward practical long-distance quantum networks, leveraging quantum error correction to mitigate imperfections in both transmission and storage.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously and robustly.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two quantum nodes are coupled to a common squeezed reservoir, which effectively mimics a squeezed environment to stabilize the entanglement. The technique uses autonomous feedback via the squeezed reservoir to continuously correct errors.
result: They experimentally demonstrate stable remote entanglement between two separate devices, showing that the entanglement persists even with realistic imperfections, and the stabilization is autonomous without active measurement or feedback.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and robust method for maintaining remote entanglement in quantum networks, which is essential for scalable quantum communication and distributed quantum computing.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully autonomous method to entangle two distant superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for quantum network entanglement distribution.
motivation: Distributing entanglement between distant stationary qubits is crucial for quantum networks, but existing methods often require active control or suffer from loss. A passive, autonomous approach using a nonlocal squeezed reservoir could provide a scalable and robust solution.
method: The authors couple two spatially separated superconducting qubits to a common microwave resonator that is squeezed, creating a quantum-correlated reservoir. The qubits interact with this reservoir, and the nonlocal correlations of the squeezed light induce entanglement between the qubits without any active measurement or feedback.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the autonomous generation of stationary entanglement between the two qubits, with a measured concurrence that confirms the presence of entanglement. The process is robust and does not require fine-tuning of qubit-reservoir coupling strengths.
conclusion: This work establishes a new, passive mechanism for entanglement distribution in quantum networks, potentially enabling high-throughput and scalable quantum communication with superconducting qubits.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel scheme for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding complex braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to provide a simpler path by leveraging non-Abelian anyons without the need for intricate braiding.
method: The method involves temporarily moving quantum information into an exotic non-Abelian phase, enabling the implementation of complex logic gates in a 2D architecture. This likely uses topological properties to achieve universality.
result: The paper demonstrates a way to perform universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D, potentially simplifying the hardware requirements and reducing overhead.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising route toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum computers by exploiting non-Abelian phases in a 2D setting.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity in diamond tin-vacancy centers coupled to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement generation for quantum networks.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity entanglement generation in scalable quantum networks, it is crucial to have efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity. This work aims to overcome previous limitations by using tin-vacancy centers in nanophotonic cavities.
method: The authors fabricate diamond photonic crystal cavities and couple individual tin-vacancy centers to them. They measure the optical properties and coherent cooperativity, and characterize the spin-photon interface.
result: They achieve above-unity coherent cooperativity, a key figure of merit for efficient spin-photon interfaces, and demonstrate the potential for high-fidelity entanglement generation.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in photonic crystal cavities as a promising platform for scalable quantum networks, with performance exceeding the threshold for high-fidelity entanglement.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To demonstrate a practical quantum computational advantage in a programmable ultracold-atom processor, going beyond proof-of-principle experiments.
method: The authors use an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely employing techniques such as Floquet engineering and measuring entanglement growth or out-of-time-order correlators to benchmark against classical simulations.
result: The processor exhibits a quantum computational advantage, showing that it can simulate the entangled dynamics more efficiently than classical methods, with quantified advantage.
conclusion: The work establishes ultracold-atom processors as a viable platform for achieving utilizable quantum advantage in simulating many-body quantum dynamics, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To provide a principled boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, addressing inconsistencies in existing criteria and uncovering potential resources for quantum technologies.
method: The authors develop a unified framework based on the process matrix formalism and generalized probabilistic theories, defining classicality in terms of the absence of certain nonclassical correlations.
result: The rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness while identifying hidden quantum features in processes long thought classical, suggesting new resources for quantum information processing.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum-classical boundary and may enable new quantum technologies by exploiting previously overlooked nonclassical properties.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to convert common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles, with applications in quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: The authors aim to overcome the challenge of generating and stabilizing multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, which is crucial for quantum sensing and simulation. They propose using dissipation, typically detrimental, as a tool.
method: They theoretically propose and analyze a scheme where spin ensembles coupled to a common cavity are driven such that the cavity dissipation leads to a steady-state entanglement. The scheme is reconfigurable, allowing different entangled states to be engineered.
result: The scheme enables robust generation of multipartite entangled states, such as spin-squeezed states, with enhanced sensitivity for quantum metrology. It also allows for the engineering of many-body states with topological properties.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway to harness dissipation for entanglement generation in hybrid systems, offering new capabilities for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD) offers advantages in integration with existing fiber networks, but achieving high secret key rates with composable security remains challenging. The authors aim to bridge this gap by combining advanced modulation with new security analysis tools.
method: The authors propose a discrete-modulated CV-QKD protocol and develop a security proof using the entropy accumulation theorem (EAT) to establish composable security against collective attacks. They optimize the modulation and detection parameters to maximize the secret key rate.
result: They demonstrate a high secret key rate over fiber optics, significantly improving over previous CV-QKD implementations while maintaining composable security. The protocol is shown to be practical and robust against realistic imperfections.
conclusion: The work brings high-speed, secure quantum networks closer to practical deployment by providing a CV-QKD protocol with both high rate and rigorous security guarantees.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity qubit readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but traditional readout methods suffer from Purcell decay and trade-offs between speed and fidelity.
method: The authors design a readout scheme exploiting nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling between the transmon and a readout resonator, which provides strong dispersive shift while suppressing Purcell decay through a bandgap-like effect.
result: They demonstrate fast (tens of ns) and high-fidelity (>99%) readout with built-in Purcell protection, outperforming conventional dispersive readout in both speed and fidelity.
conclusion: This architecture offers a promising solution for scalable superconducting qubit readout, potentially improving the performance of quantum processors.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead via parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires significant overhead in qubits and time. The goal is to reduce these overheads using advanced quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The authors employ good quantum LDPC codes, which have constant encoding rate and linear distance, and combine them with parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation, improving upon previous approaches.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a practical path towards scalable quantum computing.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify the impossibility of simulating non-projective measurements by projective ones, with experimental validation on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information protocols, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a robust and complete framework for such certification.
method: They develop a new complete SDP hierarchy that can certify the non-projectiveness of measurements, and demonstrate it experimentally using a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides a rigorous and efficient method for certification, and the experiment confirms its practical applicability.
conclusion: This work advances the theory and practice of quantum measurement certification, with implications for device-independent protocols and quantum foundations.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and information processing devices. The authors aim to establish fundamental limits on the trade-off between measurement accuracy and entropy production.
method: They introduce a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, deriving relationships between measurement accuracy and entropy production using information-theoretic and thermodynamic tools.
result: The model demonstrates a fundamental trade-off: higher measurement accuracy requires greater entropy production, quantified by a bound relating the two. This provides a general principle for the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition in quantum systems.
conclusion: The findings offer new insights into the thermodynamics of quantum measurement and have implications for the design of energy-efficient quantum detectors and information processing devices.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin ensembles that enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement, demonstrating experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: The goal is to address the challenge of controlling inhomogeneous spin ensembles for scalable quantum information processing, which is a key issue in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors develop a control framework that accounts for inhomogeneous broadening and enables global operations, and they use optically heralded entanglement to scale the system.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity operations and scalable entanglement with experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path towards large-scale quantum networks and computing using solid-state spin ensembles, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, advancing practical device-independent quantum cryptography.
motivation: Quantum random number generators are crucial for cryptographic security, but existing implementations are bulky and lack self-testing capabilities. The authors aim to miniaturize and integrate a self-testing QRNG on a photonic chip for production-scale deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that implements a self-testing quantum random number generation protocol, likely based on Bell inequality violations or quantum steering, and characterize its performance.
result: The chipset successfully generates random numbers with self-testing guarantees, demonstrating the feasibility of integrated, miniaturized device-independent quantum randomness expansion.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, compact quantum security devices, highlighting the potential for scalable deployment of self-testing quantum protocols.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric geometries for quantum tree codes, enhancing quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is limited by resource overhead and loss. Efficient tree-code generation and design are needed to make repeaters practical.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for quantum tree codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance resource usage and loss tolerance.
result: The proposed methods jointly boost quantum repeater performance, reducing resource requirements while maintaining loss tolerance, as demonstrated in simulations.
conclusion: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree codes offer a resource-efficient path toward practical quantum repeaters, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs, providing a rigorous framework for QKD device certification.
motivation: Standard security proofs for QKD often assume ideal devices, but practical implementations require characterization of device imperfections. A framework that integrates device characterization into security proofs is needed for standards and certification.
method: The authors develop a general method that incorporates device characterization into composable security proofs, likely by modeling device imperfections and deriving security bounds that account for them.
result: The method yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of QKD devices, enabling practical security guarantees.
conclusion: This work advances quantum cryptography by bridging the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device certification.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a systematic classification and analysis of quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview of available primitives and their security.
method: The authors review and classify various quantum cryptographic protocols, analyze their security guarantees and limitations, and discuss experimental implementations using photonic technologies.
result: The review presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic primitives, highlights their theoretical capabilities and constraints, and surveys current photonic experiments.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, with practical implementations emerging, though significant challenges remain in scaling and security proofs.

title: Non-Gaussianity From Superselection Rules
authors: Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, And Pérola Milman
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, and Pérola Milman

Stellar rank physically emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation to non-Gaussianity in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050203] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that stellar rank, a measure of non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable quantum systems, emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.
motivation: Non-Gaussianity is a key resource for quantum information processing, but its physical origin is not fully understood. The authors aim to provide a deeper interpretation by linking it to superselection rules and entanglement.
method: The paper uses theoretical analysis to connect stellar rank with superselection rules, likely employing group-theoretic and entanglement-theoretic tools to show how non-Gaussian states can be seen as entangled under these constraints.
result: The authors demonstrate that stellar rank can be understood as arising from superselection rules, and that this provides a new interpretation of non-Gaussianity as intrinsic multimode entanglement.
conclusion: This work offers a novel perspective on non-Gaussianity, potentially impacting quantum information processing and resource theories.

title: Deterministic Equations For Feedback Control Of Open Quantum Systems
authors: Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, and Gabriel T. Landi

Feedback control in open quantum dynamics is crucial for the advancement of various coherent platforms. However, currently only a handful of feedback master equations exist in the literature, which are restricted to specific types of feedback. In this letter we first introduce a unifying framework, …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050401] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a unifying framework for feedback control in open quantum systems, deriving deterministic master equations for various feedback types.
motivation: Feedback control is crucial for coherent platforms, but existing feedback master equations are limited to specific types. A general framework is needed.
method: The authors develop a unifying framework that encompasses existing feedback master equations and derive deterministic equations for feedback control in open quantum systems.
result: The framework provides a general approach to feedback control, potentially enabling new applications and insights in quantum thermodynamics and control.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of feedback control in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Enhancing Long-distance Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With An Error-correcting Relay
authors: S. Nibedita Swain, Ryan J. Marshman, Josephine Dias, Matthew S. Winnel, Alexander S. Solntsev, And Timothy C. Ralph
abstract:
Author(s): S. Nibedita Swain, Ryan J. Marshman, Josephine Dias, Matthew S. Winnel, Alexander S. Solntsev, and Timothy C. Ralph

Noiseless linear amplifiers serve as an effective means to enable long-distance continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD), even under realistic conditions with nonunit reconciliation efficiency. Separately, unitary averaging has been suggested to mitigate some stochastic noise, includi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012625] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an error-correcting relay using noiseless linear amplifiers and unitary averaging to enhance long-distance continuous-variable QKD under realistic conditions.
motivation: Long-distance CV-QKD is limited by noise and loss; noiseless linear amplifiers can help but are imperfect. The authors aim to improve performance by combining them with unitary averaging to mitigate stochastic noise.
method: They analyze a relay architecture that uses noiseless linear amplifiers and unitary averaging to correct errors and reduce noise, and evaluate its impact on secret key rate and distance for CV-QKD.
result: The proposed relay significantly extends the achievable distance and improves key rates compared to standard approaches, even with nonunit reconciliation efficiency.
conclusion: The error-correcting relay is a promising practical solution for long-distance CV-QKD, offering enhanced performance under realistic conditions.

title: Protocols For Sharing Genuine Multipartite Entanglement By Employing Copies Of Biseparable States
authors: Swati Choudhary, Ujjwal Sen, And Saronath Halder
abstract:
Author(s): Swati Choudhary, Ujjwal Sen, and Saronath Halder

Sharing genuine multipartite entanglement by considering the collective use of copies of biseparable states, which are entangled across all bipartitions but lack genuine multipartite entanglement at the single-copy level, plays a central role in several quantum information processing protocols, and …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012463] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents protocols for sharing genuine multipartite entanglement by collectively using copies of biseparable states, which individually lack genuine multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Genuine multipartite entanglement is a key resource for quantum information processing, but generating it from states that are only biseparable is challenging. The authors aim to show that collective use of such states can enable the sharing of genuine multipartite entanglement.
method: The authors propose protocols that employ multiple copies of biseparable states, which are entangled across all bipartitions but not genuinely multipartite entangled. They analyze the conditions under which these copies can be combined to produce genuine multipartite entanglement.
result: The protocols demonstrate that genuine multipartite entanglement can be shared using copies of biseparable states, providing a constructive method for entanglement generation in multipartite settings.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of multipartite entanglement manipulation and offers practical protocols for entanglement sharing, relevant to quantum information processing.

title: Game-theoretic Discovery Of Quantum Error-correcting Codes Through Nash Equilibria
authors: Rubén Darío Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Rubén Darío Guerrero

Quantum error-correction code discovery has relied on algebraic constructions with predetermined structure or computational search lacking equilibrium-topology analysis. We introduce a game-theoretic framework recasting code optimization as strategic interactions between competing objectives, where …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012465] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a game-theoretic approach to discover quantum error-correcting codes by modeling code optimization as a Nash equilibrium between competing objectives.
motivation: Traditional quantum error-correction code discovery relies on algebraic constructions or computational search without equilibrium-topology analysis, which may miss optimal codes.
method: The authors formulate code optimization as a strategic game where competing objectives (e.g., error correction capability and resource efficiency) are players, and use Nash equilibrium to find optimal code parameters.
result: The framework provides a new perspective on code discovery, potentially yielding novel codes and insights into the topology of code space.
conclusion: Game-theoretic methods offer a promising alternative for quantum error-correction code discovery, with potential for further exploration.

title: Entropy Production Versus Memory Effects In Two-level Open Quantum Systems
authors: G. Théret, D. Sugny, And C. L. Latune
abstract:
Author(s): G. Théret, D. Sugny, and C. L. Latune

We compare several definitions of entropy production rate introduced in the literature from a large variety of situations and motivations, and then analyze their relations with memory effects. Considering a relevant experimental example of a qubit interacting with a single bosonic mode playing the r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012456] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares different definitions of entropy production rate in open quantum systems and analyzes their relation to memory effects, using a qubit coupled to a bosonic mode as an example.
motivation: To clarify the relationship between entropy production and non-Markovianity, which is important for understanding thermodynamic costs in quantum processes.
method: The authors review and compare several definitions of entropy production rate from the literature, then apply them to a specific model of a qubit interacting with a single bosonic mode, analyzing their behavior and connection to memory effects.
result: The paper finds that different definitions of entropy production rate can lead to different conclusions about the role of memory effects, and provides insights into which definitions are most appropriate in various contexts.
conclusion: The choice of entropy production definition significantly affects the interpretation of memory effects in open quantum systems, and the study offers guidance for selecting suitable measures in thermodynamic analyses.

title: Scalable High-fidelity And Near-deterministic Preparation Of Large-photon-number States
authors: Mo Xiong, Jize Han, Chuanzhen Cao, Jinbin Li, Zhiguo Huang, And Ming Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Mo Xiong, Jize Han, Chuanzhen Cao, Jinbin Li, Zhiguo Huang, and Ming Xue

The scalable preparation of large photon-number (Fock) states is a long-standing frontier in quantum science, with direct implications for quantum metrology and bosonic quantum information processing. Despite substantial progress at small photon numbers, extending state generation to large photon nu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013721] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scalable scheme for near-deterministic preparation of large-photon-number Fock states, which is crucial for quantum metrology and bosonic quantum information processing.
motivation: Scalable preparation of large photon-number states is a long-standing challenge with direct implications for quantum metrology and bosonic quantum information processing, yet existing methods are limited to small photon numbers.
method: The authors present a scalable protocol that combines quantum non-demolition measurements and feedforward to achieve high-fidelity, near-deterministic preparation of large Fock states.
result: The scheme demonstrates high fidelity and near-deterministic preparation for large photon numbers, overcoming previous scalability limitations.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical route to generating large Fock states, advancing quantum metrology and bosonic quantum information processing.

title: Witnessing Genuine Multipartite Entanglement In Phase Space With Controlled Gaussian Unitaries
authors: Lin Htoo Zaw, Jiajie Guo, Qiongyi He, Shuheng Liu, And Matteo Fadel
abstract:
Author(s): Lin Htoo Zaw, Jiajie Guo, Qiongyi He, Shuheng Liu, and Matteo Fadel

Many existing genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) witnesses for continuous-variable (CV) quantum systems typically rely on quadrature measurements, which are challenging to implement in platforms where the CV degrees of freedom can be indirectly accessed only through qubit readouts. In this work…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012453] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a new method to witness genuine multipartite entanglement in continuous-variable systems using controlled Gaussian unitaries, which can be implemented with qubit readouts.
motivation: Existing GME witnesses for CV systems rely on quadrature measurements, which are difficult in platforms where CV degrees of freedom are accessed indirectly via qubits. The authors aim to provide a practical witness that works in such hybrid settings.
method: They introduce a witness based on controlled Gaussian unitaries and derive conditions for detecting GME, likely using phase-space representations and entanglement criteria.
result: The proposed witness can detect GME in CV systems using only qubit readouts, overcoming the limitation of quadrature measurements. It is demonstrated on specific examples.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for entanglement detection in hybrid quantum systems, relevant to quantum information and networking applications.

title: Conservative Dissipation Shapes Symmetry Breaking In Nonequilibrium Currents
authors: Matteo Sireci, Luca Peliti, And Daniel Maria Busiello
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Sireci, Luca Peliti, and Daniel Maria Busiello

Most natural thermodynamic systems operate far from equilibrium, developing persistent currents and organizing into nonequilibrium stationary states (NESSs). Yet, the general principles governing how nonequilibrium driving reshapes probability distributions and breaks equilibrium symmetries remain p…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033126] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how conservative dissipation in nonequilibrium systems shapes symmetry breaking and persistent currents, providing a general framework for understanding nonequilibrium stationary states.
motivation: Most natural systems operate far from equilibrium, yet general principles governing how driving reshapes probability distributions and breaks equilibrium symmetries remain unclear. The authors aim to uncover these principles.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework, likely using stochastic thermodynamics and symmetry arguments, to analyze how conservative dissipation (non-conservative forces) influences the emergence of nonequilibrium currents and symmetry breaking.
result: They find that conservative dissipation plays a key role in determining the structure of nonequilibrium stationary states, leading to symmetry breaking and persistent currents in a way that generalizes equilibrium phase transitions.
conclusion: The work provides a unifying perspective on nonequilibrium order and currents, with implications for understanding biological and engineered systems far from equilibrium.

title: Achieving Phase-regulated Robust Quantum Entanglement In Cavity Magnomechanics
authors: Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, And Chun-Jie Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, and Chun-Jie Yang

Generating strongly entangled states within multiparticle systems stands as a pivotal endeavor in quantum physics. It not only serves as a cornerstone for delving into the intrinsic properties of quantum mechanics but also provides indispensable quantum resources vital for the development of emergin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033102] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates robust phase-regulated quantum entanglement in a cavity magnomechanical system, a hybrid quantum platform.
motivation: Generating strong entanglement in multiparticle systems is crucial for quantum technologies, and cavity magnomechanics offers a promising hybrid platform.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a cavity magnomechanical system, deriving conditions for phase-regulated entanglement and studying its robustness against noise.
result: They show that by tuning the phase of the driving fields, robust stationary entanglement can be achieved between the magnon and mechanical modes, resilient to thermal noise.
conclusion: The work provides a practical scheme for generating robust entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, advancing quantum information processing.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence and cooperativity, and provides a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
motivation: To enhance the performance of hybrid quantum systems by understanding and mitigating loss mechanisms in multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits.
method: The authors systematically optimize the piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators and characterize the resulting phonon coherence times and cooperativity.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence time and cooperativity, and identify key loss mechanisms, leading to a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The findings provide a clear path for designing high-coherence mechanical resonators for quantum information processing, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity, enabling distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Distributed quantum computation requires reliable entanglement distribution between nodes, but physical Bell pairs are noisy and costly to purify. The goal is to prepare logical Bell pairs efficiently for fault-tolerant operations.
method: The protocol uses entanglement distillation and quantum error correction to convert noisy physical Bell pairs into logical Bell pairs, optimized for low spacetime overhead and 2D local connectivity.
result: Achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly reduced resource overhead compared to existing methods, suitable for distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: The protocol provides a practical and efficient approach for entanglement distribution in quantum networks, advancing the feasibility of distributed quantum computing.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically investigates a nonlinear cosφ coupling to suppress measurement-induced state transitions in transmon readout, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions during transmon readout limit readout fidelity, which is crucial for scalable quantum computing. The authors propose a nonlinear coupling to mitigate these transitions.
method: They combine experimental results with numerical analysis to study the dynamics of a transmon coupled via a cosφ term, comparing its performance to standard readout schemes.
result: The nonlinear coupling suppresses measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling transmon readout offers a promising approach to improve qubit readout, relevant for advancing superconducting qubit hardware.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimal resources for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity has been lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian states needed to represent a given state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank provides a unified measure that dictates the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement, and they derive bounds and examples.
conclusion: The symplectic rank offers a powerful new tool for characterizing non-Gaussianity, with implications for resource theories and quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, revealing where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental to quantum computing, and identifying regimes where quantum algorithms outperform classical ones is crucial.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum query complexity and computational complexity theory.
result: They provide new insights into the complexity landscape, showing where quantum advantage may be achievable.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum computational complexity for matrix functions, with implications for quantum algorithm design.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits with random measurements, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and introducing logical measurement statistics for stability analysis.
motivation: Understanding the stability and decodability of quantum error-correcting codes under monitored dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes, focusing on the role of measurement outcomes in decoding and introducing new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
result: They demonstrate that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and they provide new criteria for stability based on logical measurement statistics.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of monitored quantum dynamics and may inform the design of more robust quantum error-correcting protocols.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level defect in ZnO with exceptional spin properties, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: The search for new solid-state spin qubit platforms with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing and networking.
method: The authors combine first-principles calculations and experimental characterization to identify a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring its spin coherence and optical properties.
result: They find a defect with unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO defects are viable for quantum information processing, offering a new material platform for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of the continuous-variable approach to quantum communication, highlighting its advantages and recent developments.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes the state of the art in continuous-variable quantum communication, including theoretical foundations, protocol designs, and experimental demonstrations.
result: The review consolidates key results in continuous-variable QKD, quantum networking, and related protocols, emphasizing their practical relevance and security proofs.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising field with distinct advantages, and this review serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners.

title: Computational Complexity And Simulability Of non-Hermitian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Brian Barch And Daniel Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Brian Barch and Daniel Lidar

Non-Hermitian (NH) quantum systems demonstrate striking differences from their Hermitian counterparts, leading to claims of NH advantage in areas ranging from metrology to entanglement generation. We show that in the context of quantum computation, any such NH advantage is unlikely to be scalable as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033083] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the computational complexity and simulability of non-Hermitian quantum dynamics, showing that any quantum advantage from non-Hermitian evolution is unlikely to be scalable.
motivation: Non-Hermitian quantum systems exhibit unique phenomena that could potentially offer advantages in quantum computation, but the scalability of such advantages is unclear.
method: The authors study the computational complexity of simulating non-Hermitian dynamics and relate it to standard quantum computational models, possibly using complexity-theoretic reductions.
result: They find that non-Hermitian dynamics do not provide a scalable advantage over Hermitian quantum computation, and may be simulable classically under certain conditions.
conclusion: The results suggest that non-Hermitian quantum computing is not a viable path to scalable quantum advantage, aligning with the information-theoretic perspective on quantum computation.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing codes are limited. The authors aim to extend single-shot error correction to exotic topological orders, which are of fundamental interest in quantum information.
method: The authors construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes, specifically chiral color codes, and analyze their error correction properties, demonstrating single-shot capability.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, which was previously not possible with existing codes.
conclusion: This work introduces new quantum error correction codes that could enable fault-tolerant quantum computation with exotic topological orders, advancing the field of quantum error correction.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a family of scalable planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, which is a practical constraint for scalable quantum computers.
method: Designs twisted color circuits that implement non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code, and uses a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: Demonstrates a scalable family of circuits that can achieve fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder, potentially reducing overhead compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: The proposed circuits offer a promising path towards fault-tolerant universal quantum computing on planar architectures.

title: Alternative Upper Bound For Accessible Information And Wave-particle Duality
authors: Weizhe Gao And Sixia Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Gao and Sixia Yu

Accessible information of an ensemble, together with its Holevo bound, plays an essential role in quantum information science. Here, we report an alternative upper bound for accessible information based on a relation between accessible information and entanglement. Our bound can tighten the Holevo b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012466] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an alternative upper bound for accessible information that can tighten the Holevo bound, derived from a relation between accessible information and entanglement.
motivation: Accessible information is a fundamental quantity in quantum information, and the Holevo bound is a well-known upper bound. Finding tighter bounds is important for understanding the limits of information transmission.
method: The authors derive a new upper bound for accessible information based on a relation between accessible information and entanglement, likely using entanglement measures or monogamy relations.
result: The proposed bound can be tighter than the Holevo bound, providing a more precise characterization of accessible information for certain ensembles.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum information theory by offering a new tool for bounding accessible information, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Fault-tolerant non-Clifford Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Gates Using Polynomial Phase Gates And On-demand Noise Biasing
authors: Minh T. P. Nguyen And Mackenzie H. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T. P. Nguyen and Mackenzie H. Shaw

The Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) error correcting code uses a bosonic mode to encode a logical qubit and has the attractive property that its logical Clifford gates can be implemented using Gaussian unitary gates. In contrast, a direct unitary implementation of the [MATH] gate using the cubic phase …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033107] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford GKP gates using polynomial phase gates and on-demand noise biasing, advancing quantum error correction.
motivation: Direct unitary implementation of non-Clifford gates in GKP codes is challenging; the authors aim to provide a more efficient and fault-tolerant approach.
