Author(s): Alejandro Perez and Daniel Sudarsky

We analyze the expectation value of the energy-momentum tensor and its fluctuations in quantum field theory on curved spacetimes. A generally accepeted condition for the conceptual consistency of semiclassical gravity is that the fluctuations of the energy momentum tensor remain small compared to it…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051501] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tags: quantum field theory in curved spacetime
tldr: This paper analyzes the fluctuations of the quantum stress tensor in curved spacetime and argues that they impose fundamental limits on the validity of semiclassical gravity.
motivation: Semiclassical gravity, which treats gravity classically and matter quantum mechanically, requires that quantum fluctuations of the energy-momentum tensor be small. The authors aim to quantify these fluctuations and determine when they become significant enough to break the semiclassical approximation.
method: The authors compute the expectation value and fluctuations of the energy-momentum tensor in quantum field theory on curved spacetimes, likely using renormalization techniques and considering the variance of the stress tensor operator.
result: They find that the fluctuations of the stress tensor can become large relative to its expectation value in certain regimes, indicating a breakdown of semiclassical gravity and suggesting the need for a full quantum theory of gravity.
conclusion: The study establishes limits on the applicability of semiclassical gravity, highlighting the importance of quantum gravitational effects when stress tensor fluctuations are significant.
keywords: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

title: Nuclear Spin Squeezing Based On Spin-exchange Collisions
authors: He-Bin Zhang, Yuanjiang Tang, And Yong-Chun Liu
abstract:
Author(s): He-bin Zhang, Yuanjiang Tang, and Yong-Chun Liu

Isolation from the environment leads to the days-long lifetime of noble-gas nuclear spins, but also brings great challenges to the preparation, manipulation, and measurement of nuclear-spin quantum states. Here we find that nuclear spin squeezing, with an ultralong lifetime and huge atomic number, c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013725] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate nuclear spin squeezing using spin-exchange collisions, achieving ultralong-lived squeezed states in a macroscopic ensemble.
motivation: Nuclear spins have extremely long coherence times but are difficult to manipulate and measure. Generating squeezed states could enable quantum sensing and metrology with enhanced precision.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a spin-exchange collision process that correlates nuclear spins, leading to spin squeezing. They model the dynamics and quantify the achievable squeezing and lifetime.
result: They find that significant spin squeezing can be generated with an ultralong lifetime, and the large atomic number enhances the squeezing effect.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to prepare long-lived nuclear spin squeezed states, which could benefit quantum sensing and fundamental studies.

title: Quantum Target Ranging With Hetero-homodyne Detection
authors: Sangwoo Jeon, Yonggi Jo, Jihwan Kim, Zaeill Kim, Duk Y. Kim, Yong Sup Ihn, And Su-Yong Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Sangwoo Jeon, Yonggi Jo, Jihwan Kim, Zaeill Kim, Duk Y. Kim, Yong Sup Ihn, and Su-Yong Lee

Quantum target ranging, which estimates a target position using entangled photon pairs, is known to offer an error-probability advantage over classical ranging strategies. Yet, realizing this advantage in practice remains challenging, as an existing receiver design relies on collective measurements …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012462] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum target ranging protocol using hetero-homodyne detection to achieve error-probability advantage over classical strategies with practical receivers.
motivation: Quantum target ranging using entangled photon pairs offers error-probability advantages, but existing receiver designs rely on collective measurements that are difficult to implement. The goal is to design a practical receiver that retains the quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce a hetero-homodyne detection scheme for quantum target ranging, which combines heterodyne and homodyne measurements to estimate target position. They analyze the error-probability performance and compare it with classical ranging strategies.
result: The proposed hetero-homodyne detection achieves a lower error probability than classical ranging, approaching the quantum limit under certain conditions, and is more practical than collective measurement receivers.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a feasible receiver design for quantum target ranging, bridging the gap between theoretical quantum advantages and practical implementation.

title: Isogeny Graphs In Superposition And Quantum Onion Routing
authors: Eleni Agathocleous, Tobias Hartung, Karl Jansen, And Lukas Mansour
abstract:
Author(s): Eleni Agathocleous, Tobias Hartung, Karl Jansen, and Lukas Mansour

Onion routing provides anonymity by layering encryption so that no relay can link sender to destination. A quantum analog faces a core obstacle: Layered quantum encryption generally requires symmetric encryption schemes, whereas classically one would heavily rely on public key encryption. We propose…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012624] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum analog of onion routing using isogeny graphs in superposition, addressing the challenge of layered quantum encryption without public-key cryptography.
motivation: Classical onion routing relies on public-key encryption, but quantum analog requires symmetric schemes, which is a core obstacle. The paper aims to provide a quantum solution for anonymous communication.
method: The authors propose using isogeny graphs in superposition to enable layered quantum encryption, likely leveraging quantum superposition to implement the onion routing protocol.
result: The paper presents a quantum onion routing protocol that overcomes the symmetric encryption limitation, potentially enabling anonymous quantum communication.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum cryptography and quantum networks, offering a novel approach to anonymous communication in the quantum setting.

title: Berry's Phase On Photonic Quantum Computers
authors: Steven Abel, Iwo Wasek, And Simon Williams
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Abel, Iwo Wasek, and Simon Williams

We formulate a continuous-variable quantum computing (CVQC) algorithm to study Berry's phase on photonic quantum computers. We demonstrate that CVQC allows the simulation of charged particles with orbital angular momentum under the influence of an adiabatically changing [MATH] field. Alth…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012461] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a continuous-variable quantum computing algorithm to simulate Berry's phase for charged particles with orbital angular momentum in an adiabatically changing magnetic field, demonstrating a new application of photonic quantum computers.
motivation: To explore the simulation of geometric phases, specifically Berry's phase, using photonic quantum computers, which could provide insights into topological effects and quantum control.
method: The authors formulate a CVQC algorithm that maps the problem of a charged particle with OAM in a magnetic field onto a photonic quantum circuit, using continuous-variable operations to simulate the adiabatic evolution.
result: They demonstrate that CVQC can accurately simulate Berry's phase, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and highlighting the potential of photonic platforms for simulating geometric phases.
conclusion: The work establishes a new quantum simulation algorithm for Berry's phase on photonic quantum computers, contributing to the field of quantum information processing and simulation.

title: Quantum Optimal Control Of $\mathrm{Λ}$-system Ensembles
authors: Julia Cen And Domenico D'alessandro
abstract:
Author(s): Julia Cen and Domenico D'Alessandro

The quantum [MATH] system is a ubiquitous structure in many quantum technologies, where two stable, lower-energy levels are coupled indirectly via an unstable, higher-energy level that is much more susceptible to decoherence and relaxation. In this paper, we solve the problem of finding a cont…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012623] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the quantum optimal control problem for ensembles of Λ-systems, providing explicit control laws to mitigate decoherence in the excited state.
motivation: Λ-systems are ubiquitous in quantum technologies, but the unstable higher-energy level is susceptible to decoherence, limiting performance. Optimal control can improve fidelity and robustness.
method: The authors formulate the control problem for an ensemble of Λ-systems and derive analytical solutions for the optimal control fields, likely using geometric or variational methods.
result: They obtain explicit control strategies that minimize a cost functional, potentially achieving population transfer or state preparation while suppressing decoherence effects.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for optimal control of Λ-system ensembles, which could benefit quantum memory and transduction applications.

title: From Local Weight Selection To Zeno Slowdown In An Open Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain With A Single Local Loss
authors: Y. T. Wang And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. T. Wang and X. Z. Zhang

We study a quadratic open SSH chain with a single-site loss and show that the many-body fermionic Lindblad problem admits an exact reduction to a finite non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one imaginary impurity. Its rapidities generate the complete Liouvillian spectrum and reveal three mechan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012457] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an open SSH chain with local loss, showing an exact reduction to a non-Hermitian one-body matrix and revealing Zeno slowdown mechanisms.
motivation: Understanding the interplay of topology and dissipation in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing, and the SSH chain is a paradigmatic model for topological phases.
method: The authors analyze a quadratic open SSH chain with single-site loss using a many-body fermionic Lindblad master equation, reducing it to a finite non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one imaginary impurity. They compute the Liouvillian spectrum via rapidities.
result: They identify three mechanisms leading to Zeno slowdown, where the loss rate effectively suppresses dynamics, and characterize the spectral properties of the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
conclusion: The work provides exact insights into dissipative topological systems, with implications for controlling quantum dynamics via engineered losses.

title: Analysis Of The Action Of Conventional Trapped-ion Entangling Gates In Qudit Space
authors: Pavel A. Kamenskikh, Nikita V. Semenin, Ilia V. Zalivako, Vasiliy N. Smirnov, Ilya A. Semerikov, Ksenia Yu. Khabarova, And Nikolay N. Kolachevsky
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel A. Kamenskikh, Nikita V. Semenin, Ilia V. Zalivako, Vasiliy N. Smirnov, Ilya A. Semerikov, Ksenia Yu. Khabarova, and Nikolay N. Kolachevsky

Qudits, or multilevel quantum information carriers, present a promising path for scaling quantum computers. However, their use introduces increased complexity in quantum logic, necessitating careful control of relative phases between different qudit levels. In trapped-ion systems, entangling operati…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012458] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the action of conventional trapped-ion entangling gates in qudit space, focusing on phase control and gate fidelity for multilevel quantum information carriers.
motivation: Qudits offer a promising path for scaling quantum computers, but their use introduces increased complexity in quantum logic, requiring careful control of relative phases between different qudit levels. The paper aims to understand how standard trapped-ion entangling gates behave when applied to qudits.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the action of conventional trapped-ion entangling gates (such as Mølmer–Sørensen gates) on qudit states, deriving the resulting unitary transformations and phase accumulations. They likely use analytical calculations and possibly numerical simulations to characterize the gate performance.
result: The analysis reveals how the gate operations affect qudit states, including the generation of entangling operations and the dependence on qudit level spacings and laser parameters. The paper provides insights into the feasibility and limitations of using standard gates for qudit-based trapped-ion quantum computing.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that conventional trapped-ion entangling gates can be adapted for qudit operations, but careful phase control is essential. This work contributes to the development of qudit-based quantum computing in trapped-ion platforms.

title: Continuous-time Quantum Walks On A Defective Lattice: Boosting The Spreading Of Delocalized States Through Parrondo's Strategy
authors: João V. Cordeiro, Eduardo I. Duzzioni, And Edgard P. M. Amorim
abstract:
Author(s): João V. Cordeiro, Eduardo I. Duzzioni, and Edgard P. M. Amorim

We investigate the quantum transport of delocalized states in continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) on a one-dimensional lattice containing a single defect. The defect is modeled by assigning complex-valued hopping amplitudes to the edges that connect the site corresponding to the mean position of t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012459] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time quantum walks on a defective lattice, using Parrondo's strategy to enhance the spreading of delocalized states.
motivation: Quantum walks are fundamental for quantum information processing, and defects can hinder transport. The authors aim to mitigate the negative impact of a single defect on the spreading of delocalized states.
method: They model a one-dimensional lattice with a single defect by assigning complex-valued hopping amplitudes to edges connected to the defect site. They apply Parrondo's strategy, which involves alternating between two different quantum walk dynamics, to boost the spreading.
result: The Parrondo strategy significantly enhances the spreading of delocalized states compared to a single walk, effectively counteracting the defect's localization effect.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a novel application of Parrondo's paradox in quantum walks, offering a potential tool for robust quantum transport in disordered systems.

title: Phase-switchable Nonreciprocal Entanglement Via Magnon Squeezing In Ring-cavity Optomagnomechanics
authors: Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, And I. Pérez Castillo
abstract:
Author(s): Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, and I. Pérez Castillo

Cavity optomagnomechanics provides a versatile platform to explore macroscopic quantum correlations, particularly nonreciprocal entanglement. In this work we propose a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity by exploiting …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012460] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity using magnon squeezing.
motivation: To explore macroscopic quantum correlations, specifically nonreciprocal entanglement, in a cavity optomagnomechanical system, which is a hybrid quantum platform.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a ring-cavity optomagnomechanical system with magnon squeezing, deriving the quantum Langevin equations and calculating entanglement measures (e.g., logarithmic negativity) for bipartite and tripartite entanglement.
result: They find that the entanglement can be switched on/off and its direction (nonreciprocity) controlled by tuning the phase of the magnon squeezing and other parameters.
conclusion: The scheme provides a versatile platform for generating and controlling nonreciprocal entanglement, which could be useful for quantum information processing and networking.

title: Quantum Correlated Steady States Under Competing Collective And Individual Decay
authors: Nikita Leppenen And Ephraim Shahmoon
abstract:
Author(s): Nikita Leppenen and Ephraim Shahmoon

Collective dissipation can generate useful quantum correlations, while ubiquitous individual decay destroys them. We study the interplay between these two competing processes considering a driven system of many spins (“atoms”) undergoing both collective and individual dissipation (“radiation”). In t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013720] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the competition between collective and individual dissipation in a driven spin system, showing that steady states can exhibit quantum correlations despite individual decay.
motivation: Collective dissipation can generate quantum correlations, but individual decay typically destroys them. Understanding the interplay is crucial for quantum technologies.
method: The authors analyze a driven many-spin system with both collective and individual decay, likely using master equations and mean-field or exact numerical methods to characterize steady states.
result: They find that quantum correlations can persist in steady states even under competing decay processes, with conditions for their existence.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how to harness collective dissipation for quantum state preparation despite decoherence.

title: Zero-noise Extrapolation Via Cyclic Permutations Of Quantum Circuit Layouts
authors: Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, And Kirill Lakhmanskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, and Kirill Lakhmanskiy

Increasing the utility of currently available noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices requires developing efficient methods to mitigate hardware errors. In this work we propose a novel cyclic layout permutations based zero noise extrapolation (CLP-ZNE) protocol for such a task. The method le…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012620] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a novel zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) protocol using cyclic permutations of quantum circuit layouts to mitigate hardware errors on NISQ devices.
motivation: NISQ devices suffer from hardware errors, and efficient error mitigation methods are needed to improve their utility.
method: The method, CLP-ZNE, applies cyclic permutations to the circuit layout and uses zero-noise extrapolation to estimate the noiseless expectation value.
result: The protocol is demonstrated to effectively mitigate errors, improving the accuracy of quantum computations on noisy devices.
conclusion: CLP-ZNE offers a practical and efficient error mitigation technique for NISQ devices, contributing to the advancement of quantum information processing.

title: Engineering The non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model With Skin Effects In Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: J. N. Bai, F. Yang, D. Yan, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): J. N. Bai, F. Yang, D. Yan, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

We propose and systematically analyze a practical scheme for implementing a one-dimensional non-Hermitian (NH) Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model using individually addressable Rydberg atom arrays. Our setup consists of an atomic chain with three-atom unit cells, in which a synthetic gauge field is generate…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012621] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a practical scheme to implement a non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with skin effects using Rydberg atom arrays, which are a hybrid quantum platform.
motivation: The study aims to realize non-Hermitian topological phenomena, specifically the skin effect, in a controllable quantum system, leveraging the unique properties of Rydberg atoms.
method: The authors design a one-dimensional atomic chain with three-atom unit cells, using synthetic gauge fields and dissipation to engineer the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, and analyze the resulting band structure and skin effect.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed setup can faithfully reproduce the non-Hermitian SSH model with observable skin effects, and discuss parameter regimes for experimental feasibility.
conclusion: The work provides a viable route to explore non-Hermitian physics in Rydberg atom arrays, contributing to the development of hybrid quantum systems for topological and dissipative phenomena.

title: Attention In Krylov Space: Transformer-based Extrapolation Of Lanczos Coefficients
authors: Zihao Qi And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi and Christopher Earls

The Universal Operator Growth Hypothesis formulates the time evolution of operators through Lanczos coefficients. In practice, however, numerical instability and memory cost limit the number of coefficients that can be exactly computed. In response to these challenges, the standard approach relies o…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014319] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a transformer-based model to extrapolate Lanczos coefficients in Krylov space, addressing numerical instability and memory limits in computing operator growth.
motivation: The Universal Operator Growth Hypothesis requires many Lanczos coefficients, but exact computation is limited by numerical instability and memory. The authors aim to overcome these limitations by predicting coefficients beyond the computable range.
method: They employ a transformer architecture trained on exactly computed Lanczos coefficients to extrapolate further coefficients, leveraging attention mechanisms to capture patterns in the sequence.
result: The method successfully predicts Lanczos coefficients with high accuracy, enabling the study of operator growth beyond the limits of exact computation.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for investigating quantum dynamics and operator growth, potentially aiding in the analysis of thermalization and chaos in many-body systems.

title: Theory Of Single-molecule Nmr Detected By Real-time Esr
authors: Baruch Horovitz And Alexander Shnirman
abstract:
Author(s): Baruch Horovitz and Alexander Shnirman

In relation to recent experimental data [Y. Manassen et al.,
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for detecting NMR oscillations in real-time ESR data, relevant to hybrid quantum systems involving spin ensembles and microwave detection.
motivation: Recent experiments have observed sharp NMR oscillations in real-time ESR, but a theoretical understanding is lacking. The authors aim to provide a framework to demonstrate the feasibility of such detection.
method: The authors develop a theory framework that models the coupled electron-nuclear spin system and the ESR detection process, analyzing the conditions under which NMR oscillations can be observed in real-time ESR data.
result: The framework shows that sharp NMR oscillations can be detected under certain conditions, providing a theoretical basis for the experimental observations.
conclusion: The work supports the feasibility of single-molecule NMR detection via real-time ESR, contributing to the understanding of hybrid spin systems and their applications in quantum sensing and information processing.

title: Entangled Criticality And Irreversibility In Random Markov Dynamics
authors: Faheem Mosam And Eric de Giuli
abstract:
Author(s): Faheem Mosam and Eric De Giuli

We introduce a two-parameter ensemble of random discrete-time Markov models that simultaneously captures critical slowing down and broken detailed balance. Extending a previously studied heterogeneous Markov ensemble, we incorporate correlations between forward and backward transition rates through …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014315] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a random Markov ensemble with critical slowing down and broken detailed balance, studying entanglement and irreversibility in non-equilibrium dynamics.
motivation: To understand the interplay between criticality, irreversibility, and entanglement in stochastic dynamics, extending previous heterogeneous Markov models.
method: They construct a two-parameter ensemble of random discrete-time Markov models with correlated forward/backward rates, and analyze entanglement and irreversibility measures.
result: The model exhibits critical slowing down and broken detailed balance, with entanglement properties that depend on the parameters, linking irreversibility to entanglement generation.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for studying non-equilibrium critical phenomena with information-theoretic measures, relevant to quantum thermodynamics.

title: Maximum Entropy Distributions Of Wave Functions At Thermal Equilibrium
authors: Jacob T. Willson, Henrik J. Heelweg, And Adam P. Willard
abstract:
Author(s): Jacob T. Willson, Henrik J. Heelweg, and Adam P. Willard

Statistical mechanics reveals that the properties of a macroscopic physical system emerge as an average over an ensemble of statistically independent microscopic subsystems, each occupying a specific microstate. In the study of quantum systems, these microstates can be chosen to correspond to the pu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014145] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives maximum entropy distributions of wave functions at thermal equilibrium, connecting statistical mechanics with quantum state distributions.
motivation: To understand how quantum microstates are distributed at thermal equilibrium, potentially providing a new perspective on quantum statistical mechanics.
method: The authors likely use maximum entropy principles applied to wave functions, possibly within a canonical ensemble framework, to derive the distribution.
result: They obtain explicit forms for the maximum entropy distributions of wave functions at thermal equilibrium, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work offers a novel information-theoretic characterization of thermal equilibrium in quantum systems, relevant to the thermodynamics of information.

title: Convection Patterns In Nonequilibrium Kawasaki Dynamics At Low Temperature
authors: Meander van Den Brande, Kyosuke Adachi, And François Huveneers
abstract:
Author(s): Meander Van den Brande, Kyosuke Adachi, and François Huveneers

We study a conservative stochastic lattice gas (Kawasaki dynamics) coupled in the bulk to a heat bath, which leads to standard phase separation at low uniform temperatures. Instead, a macroscopic temperature gradient drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state. In this state, the usual long…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014147] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a conservative stochastic lattice gas (Kawasaki dynamics) under a temperature gradient, revealing convection patterns in a nonequilibrium steady state.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic temperature gradients affect phase separation in a stochastic lattice gas, going beyond uniform temperature behavior.
method: The authors analyze a Kawasaki dynamics model coupled to a heat bath, using theoretical and possibly numerical methods to study the nonequilibrium steady state.
result: They find that a temperature gradient drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state with convection patterns, altering the usual phase separation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium thermodynamics of lattice gases, relevant to information thermodynamics through the lens of stochastic dynamics and steady states.

title: Phase Transition From Localization To Chaos In A Classical Many-body System
authors: Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, and Tomaž Prosen

We report a dynamical phase transition in the information spreading within a classical 2D deterministic interacting many-body system. Specifically, the transition is observed in a recently introduced momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on the square lattice [Kasim and Prosen,…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014140] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a dynamical phase transition from localization to chaos in a classical many-body system, studied via information spreading in a cellular automaton.
motivation: Understanding the transition from localized to chaotic behavior in many-body systems is fundamental to statistical mechanics and may have implications for information processing and thermalization.
method: The authors analyze a momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on a square lattice, a deterministic classical many-body system, and study the spreading of information (e.g., via out-of-time-order correlators or similar measures).
result: They observe a dynamical phase transition in information spreading, indicating a sharp change from localized to chaotic behavior as a parameter is varied.
conclusion: The work provides a classical analog of quantum many-body localization-delocalization transitions, offering insights into the interplay of information dynamics and thermalization in deterministic systems.

title: Variational Simulation Of Higher-spin Systems On Qubit-based Quantum Simulators
authors: Chufan Lyu, Zuoheng Zou, Xusheng Xu, Man-Hong Yung, And Abolfazl Bayat
abstract:
Author(s): Chufan Lyu, Zuoheng Zou, Xusheng Xu, Man-Hong Yung, and Abolfazl Bayat

Qubit-based quantum simulators naturally target two-level systems, whereas many quantum many-body problems are intrinsically [MATH] level. Encodings from qudits to qubits then enlarge the Hilbert space and can introduce unphysical states that interfere with variational optimization. We formulate a vari…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033119] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) approach to simulate higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum simulators, addressing the challenge of unphysical states in qudit-to-qubit encodings.
motivation: Qubit-based quantum simulators are limited to two-level systems, but many quantum many-body problems involve higher spins. Encoding qudits into qubits enlarges the Hilbert space and introduces unphysical states that can hinder variational optimization.
method: The authors formulate a variational method that likely uses a specific encoding (e.g., binary or unary) and modifies the variational ansatz or cost function to penalize or avoid unphysical states, enabling efficient simulation of higher-spin systems.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of their variational approach through numerical simulations, showing accurate ground-state energies and fidelity for higher-spin models, and discusses resource requirements.
conclusion: The proposed variational framework provides a practical way to simulate higher-spin systems on current qubit-based quantum hardware, expanding the applicability of quantum simulators.

title: Dipolar Optimal Control Of Entangled Current States
authors: Héctor Briongos-Merino, Felipe Isaule, Bruno Juliá-Díaz, And Montserrat Guilleumas
abstract:
Author(s): Héctor Briongos-Merino, Felipe Isaule, Bruno Juliá-Díaz, and Montserrat Guilleumas

Quantum state control is a fundamental tool for quantum technologies. In this work, we propose and analyze the use of quantum optimal control to exploit the dipolar interaction of ultracold atoms on a lattice ring, focusing on the generation of selected states with entangled circulation. This scheme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033121] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum optimal control to generate entangled current states in ultracold atoms on a lattice ring via dipolar interactions.
motivation: Quantum state control is essential for quantum technologies, and generating entangled circulation states could be useful for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: The authors apply quantum optimal control techniques to exploit dipolar interactions of ultracold atoms on a lattice ring, aiming to prepare selected states with entangled circulation.
result: The scheme successfully generates the desired entangled current states, demonstrating the feasibility of optimal control in this platform.
conclusion: The work provides a method for controlled generation of entangled states in ultracold atomic systems, relevant for quantum technologies.

title: Decoherence In Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics Using Matrix Product States
authors: Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, And Stephen Hughes
abstract:
Author(s): Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, and Stephen Hughes

We present a matrix product state (MPS) method for including decoherence processes in calculations involving waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) using density matrices. The approach is based on collision quantum optics, where the many-body state of the waveguide is represented using discrete tim…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033109] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a matrix product state (MPS) method for simulating decoherence in waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) using density matrices and collision quantum optics.
motivation: Waveguide QED is a key platform for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems, but accurate modeling of decoherence is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical numerical tool for such simulations.
method: The method uses MPS to represent the many-body state of the waveguide, incorporating decoherence via a collision quantum optics approach with discrete time steps and density matrices.
result: The MPS method efficiently captures decoherence effects in waveguide QED, enabling simulations of realistic systems with moderate computational resources.
conclusion: This work offers a valuable numerical technique for studying decoherence in waveguide QED, relevant to quantum network and hybrid quantum system applications.

title: Frequency Comb Behavior Of Time Crystals In An Rf-driven Dissipative Rydberg System
authors: Dixith Manchaiah, William J. Watterson, And Christopher L. Holloway
abstract:
Author(s): Dixith Manchaiah, William J. Watterson, and Christopher L. Holloway

Driven nonlinear oscillators constitute a universal paradigm for understanding synchronization, frequency pulling, and frequency comb formation in nonequilibrium systems. Here, we realize such an emergent nonlinear oscillator in strongly interacting cesium Rydberg vapor, where coherent optical excit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033115] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates frequency comb formation in a driven dissipative Rydberg system, linking nonlinear oscillator dynamics to time-crystalline behavior.
motivation: To explore emergent nonlinear oscillator behavior in strongly interacting Rydberg vapors, which may reveal universal synchronization and frequency comb phenomena in nonequilibrium systems.
method: The authors study a cesium Rydberg vapor under coherent optical excitation and RF driving, analyzing the system's response to show frequency comb generation and time-crystal-like behavior.
result: They observe frequency comb behavior and identify conditions for time-crystalline phases, providing evidence of synchronization and frequency pulling in a dissipative quantum system.
conclusion: The work extends the paradigm of driven nonlinear oscillators to quantum many-body systems, offering insights into nonequilibrium dynamics and potential applications in quantum metrology or information processing.

title: Harnessing Subspace Controllability: Dynamical Generation Of Dicke States In Heisenberg-coupled Qubit Arrays With A Single Local Control
authors: Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, And Andrea Muratori
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, and Andrea Muratori

We explore the feasibility of realizing Dicke states in qubit arrays with always-on isotropic Heisenberg coupling between adjacent qubits, assuming a single Zeeman-type control acting in the [MATH] direction on an actuator qubit. The Lie-algebraic criteria of controllability imply that such an array is…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033095] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate Dicke states in Heisenberg-coupled qubit arrays using a single local control, leveraging Lie-algebraic controllability.
motivation: Dicke states are important for quantum information and metrology, but their generation in realistic spin chains with always-on interactions is challenging. The authors aim to achieve this with minimal control resources.
method: The authors use Lie-algebraic criteria to identify controllability of the system and design a control protocol based on a single Zeeman-type field on an actuator qubit, exploiting the subspace structure of the Heisenberg interaction.
result: They demonstrate that Dicke states can be dynamically generated with high fidelity under the given constraints, and analyze the influence of system size and coupling strengths.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to prepare multipartite entangled states in spin arrays, which is relevant for quantum simulation and sensing applications.

title: Exploring Fixed Points And Eigenstates Of Quantum Systems With Reinforcement Learning
authors: María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, And Denis Lacroix
abstract:
Author(s): María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, and Denis Lacroix

We introduce a reinforcement-learning algorithm designed to identify the fixed points of a given quantum operation. The method iteratively constructs the unitary transformation that maps the computational basis onto the basis of fixed points through a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033087] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a reinforcement-learning algorithm to find fixed points of quantum operations, which are related to eigenstates of quantum channels.
motivation: Identifying fixed points of quantum operations is important for understanding quantum channels and their long-time behavior, with applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.
method: The algorithm iteratively constructs a unitary transformation mapping the computational basis to the fixed-point basis using a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measurements.
result: The method successfully identifies fixed points for various quantum operations, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for broader applications.
conclusion: The reinforcement-learning approach offers a novel computational tool for analyzing quantum operations, with implications for quantum information processing and open quantum systems.

title: Nonreciprocal Multiphoton Bundle Emission In A Spinning Resonator
authors: Xue Gao, Jun Xu, And Xiangming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Xue Gao, Jun Xu, and Xiangming Hu

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission in a spinning resonator. The system consists of a rotating two-mode cavity directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling efficient excitation of the desired multiphoton bundle states. These photon bundles originate from leapfr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033090] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission in a spinning resonator coupled to a two-level atom, enabling directional control of multiphoton states.
motivation: The goal is to achieve nonreciprocal multiphoton emission, which is important for quantum networks and information processing, by exploiting the spinning resonator's chiral light-matter interaction.
method: The system uses a rotating two-mode cavity directly coupled to a two-level atom, and the spinning induces nonreciprocity. The authors analyze the multiphoton bundle emission via leapfrog processes and derive conditions for efficient bundle generation.
result: They demonstrate that nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission can be realized, with the direction and intensity of emission controlled by the spinning direction and system parameters.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a promising platform for generating directional multiphoton sources, which could be useful for quantum communication and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Hamiltonians Using The Sorted-list Encoding
authors: Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, and Min-Hsiu Hsieh

Quantum phase estimation is a cornerstone algorithm for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for electronic structure calculations of chemical systems. Optimal simulation relies on a complex trade-offs across many parameters including Hamiltonian simulation techniques, basis sets, and the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033091] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper benchmarks quantum simulation of chemical Hamiltonians using the sorted-list encoding, focusing on resource estimation for fault-tolerant quantum phase estimation.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation for chemical systems requires efficient Hamiltonian simulation, and the choice of encoding scheme significantly impacts resource costs. The authors aim to evaluate the sorted-list encoding as a practical option.
method: They analyze the sorted-list encoding for representing fermionic Hamiltonians, comparing its resource requirements (qubits, gates, etc.) against other encodings in the context of quantum phase estimation.
result: The paper provides detailed resource estimates and benchmarks, showing that the sorted-list encoding offers competitive or improved performance for certain molecular systems.
conclusion: The sorted-list encoding is a viable approach for quantum simulation of chemical Hamiltonians, with trade-offs that should be considered in fault-tolerant implementations.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: The spectral form factor is a key diagnostic of quantum chaos, and understanding its behavior in many-body systems is important for characterizing thermalization and chaos.
method: The authors use analytical techniques to calculate the spectral form factor, extending previous results to second order in time and covering all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order, revealing universal features and symmetry-class dependencies.
conclusion: The results deepen our understanding of quantum chaos in many-body systems and provide a benchmark for numerical and experimental studies.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, using engineered dissipation to achieve a fixed relative phase.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon with potential applications in quantum information processing and metrology, but experimental demonstrations are challenging. The authors aim to observe synchronization in a controlled quantum system.
method: They use a trapped-ion quantum simulator to implement two quantum van der Pol oscillators, engineering dissipation to induce synchronization. The synchronized state is characterized by a fixed relative phase, which is accessed through joint measurements.
result: The experiment successfully observes synchronization between the two oscillators, with the synchronized state exhibiting a fixed relative phase that is only accessible via joint measurement.
conclusion: This work provides a clear experimental demonstration of quantum synchronization in a trapped-ion platform, highlighting the role of engineered dissipation and offering a new tool for studying quantum many-body dynamics.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This review presents the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging; the process tensor offers a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: They show that tensor-network process tensors can handle a wide range of physical scenarios, providing practical tools for studying open quantum systems.
conclusion: The process tensor approach is a powerful and versatile method for non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with broad applicability in quantum thermodynamics and related fields.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces corrected product formulas that improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with minimal overhead, reducing circuit depth for a given target accuracy.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is a key subroutine in quantum algorithms, and product formulas are simple but often require deep circuits. The authors aim to enhance their efficiency without significant cost.
method: They inject carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas, correcting errors and improving the scaling of the simulation error with time.
result: The corrected formulas achieve a target accuracy with substantially lower circuit depth compared to standard product formulas, as demonstrated analytically and numerically.
conclusion: This work provides a practical improvement for Hamiltonian simulation, potentially benefiting quantum algorithms that rely on efficient simulation.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction, providing polynomial-time algorithms with rigorous error bounds and exponential convergence.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard in general, and belief propagation offers an approximate but efficient method. The authors aim to systematically improve its accuracy while maintaining polynomial complexity.
method: They propose a cluster-correction approach that adds corrections to belief propagation, enabling rigorous bounds on approximation errors and achieving exponential convergence in the correction order.
result: The method achieves polynomial-time contraction with improved accuracy over standard belief propagation, with rigorous error bounds and exponential convergence demonstrated.
conclusion: This work advances tensor network contraction algorithms, offering a practical and theoretically grounded method for quantum many-body simulations.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the advantages of using metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging the atom's small mass.
motivation: The small mass of helium-3 is expected to enable faster dynamics and stronger tunneling, which could benefit quantum simulation and continuous-variable quantum computing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and experimentally demonstrate the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays, including tunable hopping and interactions.
result: They show that helium-3 offers advantages in applications such as continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 atoms in arrays are a promising platform for quantum science, with unique advantages due to their small mass.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that operating a neutral-atom array in a cryogenic environment extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, thereby reducing errors in two-qubit gates.
motivation: Rydberg-mediated two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by finite Rydberg lifetimes, which are degraded by blackbody radiation at room temperature. Extending these lifetimes is crucial for improving gate fidelities.
method: The authors construct an optical tweezer array inside a cryogenic apparatus to shield atoms from ambient blackbody radiation, and measure Rydberg lifetimes and gate fidelities at low temperatures.
result: They observe significantly extended Rydberg lifetimes and a reduction in relaxation errors, leading to improved two-qubit gate fidelities.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable and effective strategy to mitigate Rydberg decay errors, advancing the performance of neutral-atom quantum computers.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in quantum neural networks during continual learning, showing that quantum models maintain adaptability even as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity in continual learning; the authors aim to explore whether quantum neural networks offer inherent advantages in this regard.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks in continual learning settings, comparing plasticity retention with classical counterparts, likely through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
result: They find that quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, maintaining learning capability even as the number of parameters increases, unlike classical networks.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks may provide a natural solution to the plasticity-stability dilemma in continual learning, suggesting a new avenue for quantum machine learning applications.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics, decomposing a large class of such dynamics into standard optical elements for efficient simulation.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a highly configurable and efficient approach using photonic hardware.
method: They decompose quantum field dynamics into a sequence of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters) that can be implemented on a photonic chip, enabling a configurable simulator.
result: The proposed decomposition allows for efficient execution of simulation algorithms for a broad class of quantum field dynamics, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The work offers a practical photonic platform for simulating quantum field theories, potentially advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient method for classically simulating small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, potentially using initial quantum data.
motivation: To reduce the computational cost of simulating quantum circuits by focusing on local patches of the expectation landscape, which is relevant for variational quantum algorithms.
method: The authors develop a classical surrogate model for a subregion of an expectation landscape, possibly using data from quantum computers, and analyze its efficiency.
result: They demonstrate that classically surrogating a small subregion can be done efficiently, with potential applications in quantum-classical hybrid algorithms.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to alleviate the simulation overhead in quantum computing, contributing to the field of quantum information and computation.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a cavity-QED model with kinetically constrained long-range interactions, revealing blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints and long-range interactions in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena, potentially relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: The authors introduce a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using theoretical and numerical methods to explore the phase diagram and dynamical signatures.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded superradiance and lead to long-range quantum scars, which are non-thermal eigenstates with persistent oscillations.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that cavity-QED platforms can host novel many-body phenomena, offering new avenues for quantum simulation and potentially for quantum information tasks.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-based reductions to make optimal stabilizer decompositions of multiqubit unitaries tractable, enabling classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for benchmarking and understanding quantum advantage, but optimal stabilizer decompositions are often computationally intractable for large systems.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetries of the target unitaries to reduce the search space for optimal stabilizer decompositions, making the computation feasible for larger qubit numbers.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach extends the tractable regime for optimal stabilizer decompositions beyond previous limits, enabling classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits.
conclusion: Symmetry reductions provide a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the validation of quantum devices and the study of quantum advantage.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers and exploring potential quantum advantage.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a powerful topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, but its efficient approximation is classically hard. The authors aim to provide a practical quantum algorithm that can be implemented on current and near-term quantum hardware, serving as a benchmark for quantum computational advantage.
method: The paper develops a complete algorithmic pipeline, including state preparation, quantum circuits for evaluating the Jones polynomial via the Fibonacci anyon model, and error mitigation techniques. They implement the algorithm on a trapped-ion quantum computer and compare with classical simulations.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots on real quantum hardware, demonstrating the feasibility of the approach. The results show that the quantum algorithm can achieve accurate approximations with appropriate error mitigation, and they analyze the resource requirements and potential for quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical quantum algorithm for the Jones polynomial that can serve as a benchmark for quantum computers, providing insights into the scalability and challenges of achieving quantum advantage in this problem.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:

conclusion: This work advances qubit noise spectroscopy, which is relevant for improving qubit performance in hybrid quantum systems.

method: They theoretically analyze a system of many emitters coupled to a cavity, focusing on two-photon interactions and deriving conditions for photon blockade.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced, leading to stronger antibunching and higher transmission as the number of emitters increases.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a practical route to achieve efficient photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, covering various methods and their applications across quantum physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate. A unified overview is needed to relate different approaches.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes time-propagation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems, highlighting commonalities and differences within a unified framework.
result: It presents a comprehensive overview of simulation methods, including their applicability to quantum optics, quantum information, thermodynamics, and many-body physics.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers choose appropriate simulation techniques and fosters cross-disciplinary understanding of non-Markovian dynamics.

tldr: This paper studies pole skipping in nonmaximally chaotic systems, using Rindler CFTs and the SYK chain, to probe stringy horizons.
motivation: To understand quantum chaos and its relation to black hole horizons, particularly in systems that are not maximally chaotic.
method: The authors analyze pole skipping points of few-body operators in Rindler conformal field theories and the large-q SYK chain, organizing them into trajectories in the complex frequency plane.
result: They find that pole skipping points form trajectories that may encode information about stringy horizons, extending previous work on maximal chaos.
conclusion: The study suggests that pole skipping can serve as a probe of stringy corrections to black hole horizons, even in nonmaximal chaotic systems.

conclusion: The work provides insights into the behavior of bosonic avalanche lasers, potentially relevant to quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.

The model supports degenerate zero modes that form disconnected subspaces classified by a consecutive double excitation addressing operator, with the number of subspaces growing exponentially with chain length according to a modified Fibonacci recurrence.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032015] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Hilbert space fragmentation in a driven-dephasing Rydberg atom array, leading to long-lived metastable plateaus and an effective dephasing PXP model with degenerate zero modes.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of long-lived metastable states in driven quantum systems is important for controlling quantum dynamics and potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: The authors model a resonant laser-driven chain of strongly interacting Rydberg atoms with dephasing, deriving an effective dephasing PXP model. They analyze the Hilbert space fragmentation by classifying disconnected subspaces using a consecutive double excitation addressing operator.
result: They find that the number of disconnected subspaces grows exponentially with chain length according to a modified Fibonacci recurrence, and these subspaces support degenerate zero modes leading to multiple long-lived metastable plateaus.
conclusion: The work reveals a mechanism for Hilbert space fragmentation in a dissipative Rydberg system, which may have implications for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics and potential quantum information applications.

motivation: To provide a unified low-energy description of the Bose-Hubbard model that correctly captures quantum fluctuations across the phase transition, addressing the failure of standard cumulant expansions in the superfluid phase.
method: The authors develop a field-theoretical approach, likely using path integrals or effective actions, and incorporate Berry phase effects to derive a canonical structure for quantum fluctuations.
result: They demonstrate that cumulant expansions about the Mott ground state are fundamentally inadequate in the superfluid phase, and their new framework provides a correct description of low-energy dynamics.
conclusion: The proposed field theory offers a unified description of the Mott-superfluid transition, with implications for understanding quantum fluctuations and phase transitions in correlated bosonic systems.

tldr: This paper provides an exact low-energy solution for a non-Hermitian disordered interacting Hatano-Nelson chain, showing that non-Hermiticity suppresses entanglement entropy and eliminates its scaling.
motivation: To understand the interplay of disorder, interactions, and non-Hermiticity in a one-dimensional fermionic system, particularly its thermodynamic and entanglement properties.
method: The authors solve the model exactly at low energies, likely using a mapping to a non-Hermitian spin chain and employing techniques such as bosonization or Bethe ansatz.
result: They find finite-temperature divergent spin susceptibilities and demonstrate that non-Hermiticity reduces entanglement entropy compared to the Hermitian case, removing the logarithmic scaling.
conclusion: Non-Hermiticity fundamentally alters the entanglement structure of the disordered interacting system, with implications for quantum information in non-Hermitian settings.

result: They find that SVD-based diagnostics have limitations and may not reliably locate MBL transitions in such systems.
conclusion: SVD-based diagnostics should be used with caution for non-Hermitian MBL with time-reversal symmetry, and alternative methods may be needed.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: This review covers nonequilibrium dynamics in photoexcited Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and photoinduced phase transitions.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium states in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel functionalities.
method: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing mechanisms for photoinduced dynamics and metastable states.
result: Summarizes key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of nonthermal orders like superconducting and magnetic states.
conclusion: Photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators offer rich physics but are not directly aligned with the user's core interests in quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review covers tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution, a technique in nanoscale optical imaging.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize recent advances in tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy, which combines scanning probe techniques with optical fluorescence to achieve superresolution beyond the diffraction limit.
method: The review discusses the principles of using a scanning tip as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine electromagnetic fields, and surveys experimental techniques and insights from molecular fluorescence studies.
result: The review highlights that tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy can achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution, enabling the study of electronic and vibronic properties of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: The technique offers a powerful tool for nanoscale imaging and spectroscopy, with potential applications in materials science and molecular identification.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This review paper discusses the fundamental physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the mechanisms of arcing and its impact on accelerator technology.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices, so understanding its fundamental mechanisms is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The paper synthesizes recent experimental and simulation results to present a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown, involving surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles.
result: The review provides a unified understanding of the complex interactions that trigger vacuum breakdown, offering insights for improving high-power technologies.
conclusion: Advances in experiments and simulations have led to a coherent mechanistic picture of vacuum breakdown, which can guide the development of more reliable and efficient accelerators.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications, including magnetism, topology, and spintronics.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D van der Waals magnets, which have challenged established theories and opened new applications.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D magnets, covering topics such as ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, topology, magnons, and interactions with light and electric fields.
result: The review highlights new phenomena and expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental techniques in 2D magnetism.
conclusion: The field of 2D van der Waals magnets is actively evolving, with potential for future applications in spintronics and other areas.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review on space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: To provide a unified view of quantum many-body dynamics via space-time duality, drawing analogies with quantum computation.
method: Review of theoretical concepts and results on space-time duality in lattice systems, emphasizing brickwork quantum circuits.
result: Presents a framework for understanding exactly solvable dynamics in interacting many-body systems.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful perspective for studying quantum dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.
