title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from lattice geometry and correlations.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals.
result: It highlights the role of frustration, spin-orbit coupling, and interference effects in generating novel electronic states.
conclusion: Kagome metals serve as a platform for exploring strongly correlated topological physics, but the work is primarily a materials science review without direct quantum information or thermodynamics focus.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for modeling diverse stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in physics, chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic techniques, including path integrals and quantum field theory methods, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how these methods unify various approaches and can be applied to a wide range of complex systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying framework for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes how gravitational-wave and X-ray observations of neutron stars constrain the dense matter equation of state.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties provide crucial information about the behavior of matter under extreme compression.
method: The paper reviews recent observational results from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, and compares them to theoretical predictions from nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, which are used to test and refine the nuclear equation of state at high densities.
conclusion: The review provides an outlook on future observational opportunities that will further constrain the dense matter equation of state.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiments, theory, and simulations, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research, emphasizing the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes findings from experiments, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations in spin-glass systems.
result: The review tracks progress in understanding spin-glass dynamics and highlights future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass research benefits from interdisciplinary collaboration, and the field continues to offer open questions.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic states of matter with potential applications in quantum computing, but their realization is challenging.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev model) and experimental progress in candidate materials.
result: Summarizes key properties such as chiral edge modes and identifies leading candidate materials.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive overview for researchers, highlighting open questions and future directions.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review connects statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to large-scale neural recordings, aiming to uncover reproducible collective behaviors in brain networks.
motivation: The authors aim to bridge theoretical statistical physics with quantitative neuroscience experiments to find universal principles in neural network activity.
method: The paper reviews recent work applying maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to multi-neuron recording data.
result: It highlights that these methods reveal reproducible, quantitative behaviors in neural networks, suggesting that abstract physical principles can have predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: The review argues for the value of statistical physics approaches in understanding brain function, but it is not directly aligned with the specified research directions.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on photophysical processes.
motivation: To understand and model nonradiative transitions in molecules and materials, relevant to photonics and energy harvesting.
method: Reviews various theoretical approaches for describing internal conversion, including quantum dynamics and rate theories.
result: Summarizes current methods and their applicability to applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
conclusion: Provides an outlook on incorporating these models into practical studies, but does not present new results.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To provide an overview of quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics and quantum technologies.
method: A review article summarizing theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum properties, including interactions and quantum dynamics.
result: The paper discusses quantum effects in skyrmion formation and the possibility of skyrmions exhibiting quantum behavior, but does not present new research findings.
conclusion: Skyrmions may offer a platform for studying quantum topological phenomena, but the paper is a review without novel contributions to the user's specific research directions.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, potentially mediated by new bosons and relevant to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To consolidate the state of the art in searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions, which could reveal new physics beyond the standard model and shed light on dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper is a review that summarizes theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and surveys experimental techniques used to search for them.
result: The review catalogs various theoretical models and experimental constraints, highlighting the current status and future prospects for detecting such interactions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, with ongoing experimental efforts and theoretical developments.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining that apparent violations arise from violating assumptions in the bounds' derivation.
motivation: To clarify why some measured material properties exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how designing materials to violate these assumptions can yield interesting properties.
method: The paper is a review (Colloquium) that surveys various circumstances where measurements exceed thermodynamic bounds and identifies which underlying assumptions are violated in each case.
result: It catalogs many examples of apparent violations and explains the assumptions behind them, also discussing how to engineer materials to exploit these effects.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but result from misapplied assumptions; understanding this can guide the development of novel materials.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical approaches to simulating quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries such as fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology, potentially revealing new physics.
method: The paper surveys implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems, discussing theoretical frameworks and experimental techniques for realizing these geometries.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current capabilities and challenges in simulating quantum matter in nonstandard geometries.
conclusion: The field is promising for advancing quantum simulation, but the paper is a review without novel technical contributions directly aligned with the specified research directions.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: This review explores self-alignment in active matter systems, where particles align their orientation with their velocity, leading to novel collective behaviors.
motivation: The paper aims to unify and understand the role of self-alignment in active matter, which is a key mechanism in biological and synthetic systems.
method: It provides a comprehensive review of existing models and experiments, introducing a unified mathematical and conceptual framework for self-alignment.
result: The review highlights how self-alignment leads to phenomena such as orbiting in traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies, and discusses potential applications.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental property that reshapes active matter dynamics, offering new avenues for research and applications in biology, materials, and robotics.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This review covers nonlinear elasticity theory for buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to provide a modern treatment of the Biot instability in soft matter, integrating nonlinear physics and solid mechanics techniques.
method: It reviews bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and integral methods applied to nonlinear elasticity.
result: The review synthesizes existing knowledge on crease and cusp formation in growing soft materials.
conclusion: The work is a contribution to soft matter physics and mechanics, not to the user's research directions.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: This review paper discusses experimental and theoretical efforts to probe gravity using massive quantum systems, focusing on decoherence and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: The authors aim to review the current state of research on testing gravity's quantum effects using massive quantum systems, as classical gravity is poorly tested and quantum probes may reveal new physics.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical proposals and experimental state-of-the-art for studying gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement in massive quantum systems.
result: The review summarizes ongoing experiments and theoretical frameworks for detecting quantum gravitational effects, such as gravity-mediated entanglement and collapse models.
conclusion: The authors conclude that experiments testing quantum gravity effects are underway and will guide future theoretical descriptions of gravity at the quantum scale.

title: Magnetocubic And Magnetolinear Dependence Observed In The In-plane Anomalous Hall Magnet ${\mathrm{EuCd}}_{2}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{2}$
authors: Ayano Nakamura, Shinichi Nishihaya, Mitsuru Akaki, Motoi Kimata, Kenta Sudo, Yuki Deguchi, Hsiang Lee, Tadashi Yoneda, Markus Kriener, Masaki Kondo, Hiroaki Ishizuka, Masashi Tokunaga, And Masaki Uchida
abstract:

The Hall effect under in-plane magnetic field has emerged as a sensitive probe of quantum geometric properties in solids. In trigonal systems, the in-plane anomalous Hall effect (AHE) originates from unconventional off-diagonal coupling between the magnetic field and the Hall vector on the principal…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051112] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental observations of magnetocubic and magnetolinear dependences in the in-plane anomalous Hall effect of the magnetic material EuCd2Sb2.
motivation: The study aims to probe quantum geometric properties in solids via the in-plane anomalous Hall effect, which is a condensed matter physics topic.
method: The authors performed Hall effect measurements under in-plane magnetic fields on EuCd2Sb2 and analyzed the field dependence.
result: They observed magnetocubic and magnetolinear dependences in the in-plane anomalous Hall effect.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the quantum geometric properties of this material, but the work is primarily experimental condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamics Of Particle Lane Formation In Confined Viscoelastic Fluids Under Shear
authors: Hiroto Yokoyama, Masanori Honda, Rinya Miyakawa, Yuki Shinohara, Kota Nakamura, Kojiro Otoguro, Kiwamu Yoshii, And Yutaka Sumino
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroto Yokoyama, Masanori Honda, Rinya Miyakawa, Yuki Shinohara, Kota Nakamura, Kojiro Otoguro, Kiwamu Yoshii, and Yutaka Sumino

Simple shear flow can induce flow-aligned chain formation of particles suspended in viscoelastic fluids. Although this phenomenon has been reported for decades, direct in situ measurements of the alignment dynamics and particle trajectories during chain formation remain limited. Here, we develop an …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015422] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of particle chain formation in viscoelastic fluids under shear, a topic in soft matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to provide direct in situ measurements of particle alignment dynamics during chain formation in viscoelastic fluids, which has been limited despite decades of reports.
method: They develop an experimental setup to measure particle trajectories and alignment dynamics in a confined viscoelastic fluid under simple shear flow.
result: The paper presents new experimental data on the dynamics of particle lane formation, likely revealing mechanisms of chain alignment.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding particle behavior in complex fluids, but are outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: Role Of Manifolds In The Transport Of Chaotic Trajectories In The Standard Nontwist Map
authors: Michele Mugnaine, Matheus Rolim Sales, Edson Denis Leonel, Iberê Luiz Caldas, And José Danilo Szezech, Jr.
abstract:
Author(s): Michele Mugnaine, Matheus Rolim Sales, Edson Denis Leonel, Iberê Luiz Caldas, and José Danilo Szezech, Jr.

A crucial question in transport theory is determining the critical parameter values at which abrupt changes in phase space occur. In nontwist Hamiltonian systems, this transition is associated with the breakup of the shearless curve. Ideally, once this curve is destroyed, chaotic trajectories should…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014222] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chaotic transport in a nontwist Hamiltonian map, focusing on the role of manifolds in the breakup of the shearless curve.
motivation: Understanding critical parameter values where abrupt changes in phase space occur is crucial in transport theory, particularly for nontwist Hamiltonian systems.
method: The authors analyze the standard nontwist map, examining the dynamics of chaotic trajectories and the role of stable and unstable manifolds in transport.
result: The paper identifies how manifolds influence the transport of chaotic trajectories, particularly around the breakup of the shearless curve.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of transport barriers in Hamiltonian systems, but the topic is far from the user's research interests.

title: Short-term Plasticity-based Working Memory Spiking Model Is Resilient To Synaptic Heterogeneity
authors: Gianmarco Tiddia, Luca Sergi, Simone Rubiu, Antonio Incollu, And Bruno Golosio
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmarco Tiddia, Luca Sergi, Simone Rubiu, Antonio Incollu, and Bruno Golosio

The presence of activity-silent working memory has been increasingly supported by experimental observation, and short-term synaptic facilitation is suggested to underlie this phenomenon. Originally proposed in the early 2000s, the synaptic theory of working memory was supported by a relatively simpl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014409] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a spiking neural network model of working memory based on short-term synaptic plasticity, and shows it is resilient to synaptic heterogeneity.
motivation: The study aims to support the synaptic theory of working memory by demonstrating that a biologically plausible spiking model can maintain activity-silent memory despite variability in synaptic parameters.
method: The authors construct a spiking neural network model with short-term facilitation and simulate its behavior under heterogeneous synaptic conditions, likely using computational neuroscience techniques.
result: The model exhibits robust working memory performance even with significant synaptic heterogeneity, suggesting that short-term plasticity provides a resilient mechanism.
conclusion: The findings reinforce the plausibility of short-term synaptic facilitation as a basis for working memory, with implications for understanding neural computation.

title: Generating Consensus And Dissent On Massive Discussion Platforms With A Semantic-vector Model
authors: Alfredo Ferrer, David Muñoz-Jordán, Alejandro Rivero, Alfonso Tarancón, Carlos Tarancón, And David Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): Alfredo Ferrer, David Muñoz-Jordán, Alejandro Rivero, Alfonso Tarancón, Carlos Tarancón, and David Yllanes

Reaching consensus on massive discussion networks is critical for reducing noise and achieving optimal collective outcomes. However, the natural tendency of humans to preserve their initial ideas constrains the emergence of global solutions. To address this, collective intelligence (CI) platforms fa…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014311] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a semantic-vector model to simulate consensus and dissent dynamics on massive discussion platforms, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to address the challenge of reaching consensus in large-scale online discussions, where human tendency to preserve initial ideas hinders collective outcomes.
method: They introduce a semantic-vector model that represents opinions as vectors and simulates interactions to study consensus and dissent emergence.
result: The model likely demonstrates conditions for consensus or polarization, but the abstract is truncated; no specific quantitative results are provided.
conclusion: The paper contributes to collective intelligence and opinion dynamics, but has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics and chemistry of transplutonium compounds under high pressure, focusing on their electronic structure and behavior.
motivation: Transplutonium materials are important for nuclear applications and exhibit unique electronic properties due to 5f electrons, but their high-pressure behavior is not well understood.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, compounds, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: The review highlights the complex interplay between localized and itinerant 5f electrons, leading to diverse phenomena under pressure.
conclusion: Understanding pressure effects on transplutonium materials is crucial for nuclear science and reveals fundamental aspects of actinide chemistry.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection methods, focusing on multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave predictions, as well as detection strategies for ground-based interferometers.
method: It provides a review of supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, along with an overview of detection methods and parameter estimation techniques.
result: The paper presents the current state of the art in predicting gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and discusses how to detect them in multimessenger observations.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of gravitational wave detection from nearby supernovae for understanding the explosion mechanism and neutron star physics.

title: Light Dark Matter Search With 7.8 Tonne-Year Of Ionization-Only Data In XENONnT
authors: E. Aprile et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): E. Aprile et al. (XENON Collaboration)

World-leading bounds are placed on sub-keV axionlike and dark-photon dark matter using ionization-only data from a liquid xenon detector.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051003] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports world-leading bounds on sub-keV axionlike and dark-photon dark matter using ionization-only data from the XENONnT liquid xenon detector.
motivation: The search for light dark matter candidates such as axionlike particles and dark photons is a key goal in particle physics, and liquid xenon detectors offer high sensitivity to their ionization signatures.
method: The XENONnT detector collected 7.8 tonne-years of ionization-only data, and the analysis searched for excess events that could be attributed to dark matter interactions, using a profile likelihood approach.
result: No significant excess was found, and the analysis set world-leading exclusion limits on sub-keV axionlike and dark-photon dark matter.
conclusion: The results significantly constrain light dark matter models, demonstrating the power of large-scale liquid xenon detectors for such searches.

title: Static Friction Of Liquid Marbles
authors: Yui Takai, Kei Mukoyama, Pritam Kumar Roy, Guillaume Lagubeau, David Quéré, Samuel Poincloux, And Timothée Mouterde
abstract:

Liquid marbles, droplets coated with a granular layer, are highly mobile as particles prevent capillary adhesion to the substrate. Yet their coating creates a static rolling friction, which we measure and model. Motion requires shear within the shell so that it is governed mainly by the grain densit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 054001] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the static rolling friction of liquid marbles, which are droplets coated with granular particles, and models how grain density affects their motion.
motivation: Understanding the frictional properties of liquid marbles is important for applications in microfluidics and transport, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors experimentally measure the static rolling friction of liquid marbles and develop a model based on shear within the granular shell, relating friction to grain density.
result: They find that motion requires shear within the shell and that friction is mainly governed by grain density, providing a quantitative model.
conclusion: The study advances the physics of liquid marbles but has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information science.

title: First-Principles Predictions Of Carrier Mobility With Record Accuracy Using Gw Perturbation Theory
authors: Nick Pant, Sabyasachi Tiwari, Steven G. Louie, Zhenglu Li, And Feliciano Giustino
abstract:

Accurate prediction of carrier mobility is critical for the discovery and design of next-generation electronic materials. Despite sustained progress, state-of-the-art ab initio methods remain limited by the approximate treatment of electron-phonon interactions at the density functional theory level.…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056303] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a first-principles method for predicting carrier mobility with record accuracy using GW perturbation theory.
motivation: Accurate prediction of carrier mobility is critical for discovering next-generation electronic materials, but current ab initio methods are limited by approximate treatment of electron-phonon interactions at the DFT level.
method: The authors develop a GW perturbation theory approach to compute carrier mobility from first principles, improving upon DFT-based methods.
result: The method achieves record accuracy in predicting carrier mobility for materials.
conclusion: The proposed GW-based approach significantly advances the predictive capability for carrier mobility, aiding materials discovery.

title: Boiling After The Dust Settles: Constraining First-Order Phase Transitions During Dark Energy Domination
authors: Seth Koren, Yuhsin Tsai, And Runqing Wang

A first-order phase transition could occur in the late Universe when vacuum energy begins dominating the energy density ([MATH]) and convert some latent heat into other forms such as invisible radiation. This generic possibility also has concrete motivation in particle physics models, which invoke …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051002] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-order phase transitions during dark energy domination, a topic in cosmology and particle physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to constrain the possibility of first-order phase transitions occurring in the late Universe when vacuum energy dominates, motivated by particle physics models.
method: They analyze the cosmological implications of such phase transitions, likely using theoretical models and constraints from observations.

title: Multimessenger Signatures Of Tilted, Self-Gravitating, Black Hole Disks
authors: Milton Ruiz, Antonios Tsokaros, And Stuart L. Shapiro
abstract:
Author(s): Milton Ruiz, Antonios Tsokaros, and Stuart L. Shapiro

We perform fully relativistic general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamics simulations of magnetized, self-gravitating black hole disk (BHD) systems in which the black hole spin is misaligned with the disk angular momentum. Massive disks (disk to black hole mass ratios of 16%–28%) around rapidly rotati…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051402] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.

abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.

conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle, potentially requiring modifications to the standard model of cosmology.

authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental constraints and discovery potential.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, and recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space, motivating a survey of viable models and future search prospects.
method: The paper is a review that surveys current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and presents projections for discovery potential across multiple search channels and scenarios.
result: It provides an overview of the status of supersymmetry and outlines the expected sensitivity of the HL-LHC to various supersymmetric models.
conclusion: The paper concludes that while supersymmetry remains viable, the HL-LHC will provide crucial tests, but the topic is outside the user's research interests.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses optoacoustic microscopy, an imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to visualize biological tissues, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to provide an overview of optoacoustic imaging, its physics, and its applications in biological and clinical research.
method: It is a review article summarizing the basic physics, recent developments, and multimodal approaches in optoacoustic microscopy.
result: The review highlights the capabilities of optoacoustic imaging for deep tissue imaging with high resolution and discusses its impact on biological and clinical research.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a powerful imaging tool, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information science.
